media_strategy.selection_principle: Chart-led blog driven by tabular pharmacovigilance data. Channels are kept honest: one atmospheric image (teaser) + image2video animation; chart for every load-bearing finding; one interactive quiz where the reveal carries the story; one interactive map for geographic data; one data sonification synced to the daily-volume chart. No additional decorative images or videos — det_10 explicitly warned against generic medical stock imagery.

chart.reason: The dataset is structured quantitative comparisons across drugs, reactions, demographics, and time. Charts are the only honest way to show ranking and concentration.

image.reason: One editorial still image as the page opener — a stack of medical safety reports with one glowing — sets the megaphone metaphor that frames the whole piece. Detective explicitly cautioned against generic medical imagery (det_10), so additional images are intentionally avoided.

video.reason: image2video on the teaser still — a slow parallax push with a heartbeat-pulse of warm light from below. The motion is the only video element; it animates the page opener rather than fabricating an event.

audio.reason: Data sonification of the 54-day daily-volume time series (ana_29). Each day becomes a brief tone — high pitch on weekdays, drop-out on weekends — synced with the daily-volume chart so the reader sees and hears the bureaucratic rhythm simultaneously. Implemented with Web Audio API in the Programmer's HTML, not a generated WAV, so the sonification is exactly the data.

interactive_or_map.reason: Two interactives: (a) a guess-first quiz at edt_01 — 'which of these is the most-reported reaction?' — that turns the surprising lead into a reveal; (b) a Leaflet world map at edt_07 showing reports per occur-country with the U.S. dominance visible at a glance.

des_teaser_image.label: Teaser hero — glowing stack of medical reports

content.prompt: Editorial overhead photograph of a thick stack of paper medical safety reports sitting on a dark matte slate surface, one report at the top glowing with a soft warm orange light from below, dramatic single-source lighting from upper left, shallow depth of field, muted desaturated palette of charcoal and steel-grey with a single warm accent, top-down composition, no text or words visible anywhere in frame, no logos, no faces, conceptual photography style, 16:9 aspect

des_teaser_image.brief: Static fallback image of a stack of safety reports — the topmost a chest x-ray — with warm light pulsing from beneath. Used as the poster frame for the teaser video and as the no-JS fallback.
des_teaser_image.rationale: A single atmospheric still establishes the FAERS-as-megaphone metaphor before any data appears. No people, no drugs in frame — keeps the conceptual frame clean.

des_teaser_video.label: Teaser motion — image2video animated hero

content.prompt: very slow parallax push-in toward the topmost chest x-ray report, faint warm light from underneath the stack subtly pulses brighter and dimmer like a heartbeat, gentle drift of fine dust motes in the air, no camera shake, no other motion, dark editorial mood

des_teaser_video.brief: Six-second loopable clip — the teaser_hero still with a slow parallax push and a heartbeat-pulse of warm light from beneath the topmost report. Autoplays muted, loops; poster = teaser_hero.png so the no-JS case still shows the image.
des_teaser_video.rationale: image2video preserves the composition we already invested in for the still and adds the kinetic feeling of a 'live' database without inventing fake content. Pulse rhythm visually echoes the weekday/weekend heartbeat sonification later in the page.

des_01_quiz.label: Guess-first: which 'reaction' is most-reported?

content.initial_state: Four large clickable cards in a 2x2 grid, each showing one candidate MedDRA term: 'Nausea', 'Death', 'Off label use', 'Headache'. The prompt above reads: 'Out of 600,000 reaction rows in FAERS 2024, which one was reported most often?'
content.transition: All four cards flip simultaneously to reveal each term's actual count and percentage; the correct card pulses with a warm-orange glow that matches the teaser; a small caption under the grid shows whether the reader was right
content.payoff: The reveal: 'Off label use — 14,801 mentions, 2.48%. The most-reported 'reaction' in FAERS is not a medical event.' A short follow-up sentence makes the connection to the rest of the piece.

des_01_quiz.brief: 2x2 card grid quiz. Reader commits to a guess; all four cards flip to reveal counts; 'Off label use' pulses orange when revealed. Designed so even readers who get it right have to confront how non-medical the top of the list is.
des_01_quiz.rationale: The finding is genuinely counter-intuitive. A passive bar chart would let the eye skip the surprise; a quiz makes the reader spend a moment with the wrong intuition first.

des_01_chart.label: Top 30 MedDRA reactions — horizontal bar

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing exact count and pct_of_reaction_rows; clicking a bar opens a small inline panel with that term's definition

style.palette: neutral grey with three warm-orange bars for highlighted non-medical/meta terms
style.value_labels: show count at the end of each bar

des_01_chart.brief: Horizontal bar chart of the top 30 reactions, sorted by frequency. Most bars are neutral grey; the three non-medical/meta terms ('Off label use', 'Drug ineffective', 'Death') are warm-orange to make the editorial point visible at a glance.
des_01_chart.rationale: Shows the full ranked tail so the reader can see how flat the distribution is after the top three, and how many recognisably-medical terms are nested among non-medical ones.

des_02_callouts.label: FAERS-at-a-glance stat strip
des_02_callouts.brief: Four large stat callouts in a single horizontal strip, each with a value, a label, and a short caveat-note in smaller type. Designed to anchor the 'no denominator, no rate' point with concrete numbers.
des_02_callouts.rationale: edt_02 is pure context — no chart needed, but the reader needs the headline magnitudes before the rest of the blog lands. Stat callouts do this without bloat.

des_03_chart.label: Top 25 most-reported drugs

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing exact row count and percentage of all drug rows

style.palette: muted navy bars; Dupixent and Mounjaro in a brighter teal; Ozempic and Zepbound in warm-orange for the GLP-1 setup
style.value_labels: show count at the end of each bar

des_03_chart.brief: Horizontal bar chart of the top 25 most-reported drugs. Dupixent and Mounjaro share the top of the chart in a brighter teal; Ozempic and Zepbound carry a warm-orange that sets up the GLP-1 narrative for the next section. Generic-name annotations to the right of each bar.
des_03_chart.rationale: A single chart that does both jobs: it ranks the top drugs (the explicit edt_03 finding) and pre-loads the GLP-1 thread the next section unpacks.

des_04_chart.label: GLP-1 brand head-to-head — grouped bars

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing exact percent, deaths, and report count for that brand

style.palette: three-color grouped bars; brand labels in a fixed left column

des_04_chart.brief: Eight GLP-1 brands as rows, three metrics each (Serious %, Hospitalization %, Death %) as grouped horizontal bars. Annotated with report counts so the reader can scale interpretation. Zepbound's near-zero bars make the visual point of the section.
des_04_chart.rationale: A grouped horizontal bar is the cleanest format for three small metrics across many brands. The visual asymmetry — Saxenda's huge serious bar at the bottom, Zepbound's nearly invisible bars at the top — does the editorial work without prose.

des_04_secondary.label: GLP-1 class share by molecule — donut

content.interaction: hover tooltip with exact rows and percentage of GLP-1 class

style.palette: five-color sequential — tirzepatide warm-orange, semaglutide cool blue, others greyscale

des_04_secondary.brief: Small donut chart breaking the 26,170 GLP-1 drug rows into the five molecules. Tirzepatide visibly larger than semaglutide.
des_04_secondary.rationale: Donut placed inline with the head-to-head chart shows the class-share story (tirzepatide 3.3x semaglutide) in one glance.

des_05_chart.label: Mounjaro vs Ozempic top reactions — side-by-side

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing count and percentage

des_05_chart.brief: Two side-by-side panels (Mounjaro left, Ozempic right), each showing the brand's top 12 reactions as horizontal bars. Bars colored by category: device/dosing complaints in warm orange, biological symptoms in teal, meta terms in grey. The visual contrast — orange-dominated Mounjaro panel vs teal-dominated Ozempic panel — IS the finding.
des_05_chart.rationale: Side-by-side faceting reads instantly. Coloring by reaction category makes the device-vs-body story visible without prose.

des_05_lift.label: GLP-1 over-represented reactions — lollipop

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing glp1_count, glp1_pct, overall_pct, lift

style.palette: neutral grey lollipops with five accent-orange dots for highlighted terms
style.value_labels: show lift value at the dot end

des_05_lift.brief: Lollipop chart of the 20 reactions most over-represented in GLP-1 reports vs the dataset average. Highlight five terms — Weight loss poor, Increased appetite, Hunger, Impaired gastric emptying, Pancreatitis — to surface the class paradox plus the known pancreatitis signal.
des_05_lift.rationale: Lollipop reads cleanly for lift values that range 5x to 21x. Highlights act as silent annotations.

des_06_chart.label: Death-rate hotspot drugs — diverging bar

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing n_reports, deaths, death_pct, hosp_pct

style.value_labels: show death pct at end of bar

des_06_chart.brief: Horizontal bar chart of the top 20 drugs by share of suspect-reports tagged with seriousnessdeath, colored by drug class. The dark-red top of the chart (methamphetamine, alcohol, fentanyl) makes the 'overdose signature, not weight-loss drugs' point visually.
des_06_chart.rationale: Color-by-class converts an otherwise inscrutable ranking into an instant pattern: the top of the list is overdose drugs.

des_07_chart_daily.label: Daily report volume — bar chart, weekend-shaded

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing date, day-of-week, and reports

des_07_chart_daily.brief: Vertical bar chart of all 54 days in the window. Weekday bars in teal, weekend bars in warm red — the visual rhythm IS the finding. Two annotations point at a representative Friday/Saturday cliff.
des_07_chart_daily.rationale: Color-coding by day-of-week category makes the weekday/weekend rhythm visible without a faceted chart.

des_07_sonification.label: Sonification: hear the 54-day FAERS heartbeat

content.why_audio: The weekday/weekend pattern is a rhythmic finding. Hearing 54 short tones in 5 seconds — high pitches on weekdays, near-silence on weekends — makes the bureaucratic heartbeat physically obvious in a way a bar chart cannot.
content.trigger: User clicks a small 'Play the 54-day rhythm' button below the daily-volume chart
content.ui_form: chart-synced sonification — as each tone plays, the corresponding bar in the daily-volume chart pulses brighter for ~80ms

content.implementation: Web Audio API in the Programmer's HTML — no generated WAV. Each day maps to a 90ms sine-wave tone; pitch = 220 Hz + (reports / max_reports) * 660 Hz (so the loudest day is ~880 Hz). Weekend tones use a softer triangle wave at low volume to create audible drop-out.

content.fallback: If the user does not click play, or audio is unsupported, the daily-volume chart alone communicates the finding via its red/teal color rhythm. No autoplay.
content.novelty_note: Not a click-to-play tone card. The tones are synced bar-by-bar with a chart and the legend explains the pitch mapping so the reader knows exactly what they are hearing.

des_07_sonification.brief: Play button under the daily-volume chart. Click triggers 54 ~90ms tones, one per day, pitch-mapped to report count. Weekend days near-silent; weekday days clearly audible. Bar pulses brighter during its tone.
des_07_sonification.rationale: The data has 54 ordered values — exactly the kind of small ranked sequence sonification handles well. Synced with the chart so the audio is interpretable rather than decorative.

des_07_map.label: Where the events occur — Leaflet world map

content.interaction: hover/click a country to see exact report count and percentage; the U.S. is highlighted with a small static annotation: '120,528 reports — 60.3% of the sample'
content.scope_note: Show only the top 15 countries plus a 'rest of world' bucket; small countries with fewer than 1000 reports are visible but not the focus.

des_07_map.brief: Leaflet world map (CARTO Voyager basemap), choropleth-colored by occur-country report count on a log scale. U.S. labeled with the dominant-share annotation. Hover any country for exact counts. Reader can zoom and pan.
des_07_map.rationale: The data has a real ISO-3166 country code dimension. Geography is the most honest visualization for it — a non-spatial chart would lose the punchline that one country has 60% of the world's submissions.

des_07_sex_inline.label: Sex skew — inline waffle/bar

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing each share's count and percent

des_07_sex_inline.brief: Single thin horizontal stacked bar split into four segments by patient sex. Sized to fit inside the prose column at 24px tall. Used as an inline visual rather than a full chart.
des_07_sex_inline.rationale: The sex skew is one number, not a distribution — a thin stacked bar is the lightest-weight way to show it without breaking the section's rhythm.

des_08_pullquote.label: Closing pull quote

content.value: FAERS is a megaphone, not a measurement.
content.label: the rule of thumb for every headline about an adverse-event-database surge

des_08_pullquote.brief: Italic serif pull quote in large display type, with a smaller caption below. Used in place of a final chart — the closing section is editorial, not data-driven.
des_08_pullquote.rationale: The blog needs a sentence the reader can carry away. A pull quote at the close does this without forcing one more chart.

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial — charcoal background, off-white type, warm-orange and teal accents
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: alternating: opener (image+video) → quiz → chart → stat strip → chart → chart → side-by-side chart + lollipop → diverging bar → daily-volume chart + sonification + map → pull quote close
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: Lead with a reader-quiz instead of a chart so the surprise is felt before it is shown; avoid the standard 'click-to-play tone card' by binding the sonification to the chart it explains; intentionally skip extra generated images per det_10 (no generic pill-bottle stock photos).
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Display headings in 40px geometric sans; stat callouts at 64px with 14px caveat-notes; pull quote at 32px italic serif; body at 17px with generous leading. Section dividers are thin warm-orange rules, not horizontal lines. Charts inherit the page's dark palette — no separate chart-card backgrounds.
